MX17 resistive-strip micromegas · the reconstruction's forward model · 16 Oct 2026

A physical detector model replaces the fitted copy kernel: drift diffusion, a readout footprint, and RC spreading along the resistive strips.

Every constant is measured on head-on tracks (bench and beam), none is fitted to the angle. With no refit, the Y angle improves on all five bench chambers. X does not close yet.

5 / 5

chambers with a better Y angle, no refit

Y s68 -0.09 to -0.55° on all tracks, -0.14 to -0.90° head-on.

5 → 1

fitted sharing constants replaced by one measured D_rc

c1, c2, kY, τ_s, σ_s become a resistive-strip diffusion constant on Y; X has none.

X: open

the X width grows faster than the gas allows

det4 X is worse, X χ² is worse everywhere, and the kernel is not frozen.

1

Details

What this note is. The waveform reconstruction (wft/) fits every strip's sampled signal with a forward model: given a track's position, inclination and start time, it predicts each strip's waveform and solves the charge per drift-depth slice by NNLS. How charge reaches a strip's neighbours is the part of that model that sets the angle. Until October it was a fitted copy kernel (c1, c2, kY, τ_s, σ_s on top of a Gaussian σ_p0 and a drift term Dp). The cloud_basics study (FINDINGS §1–29) replaced it, piece by piece, with physics measured directly on head-on tracks.

Part 1 (slides 2–10) explains the new model on its own, in the order the charge travels. Part 2 (11–16) sets it against the old kernel and shows what the held-out bench says. Slides 17–19 are what is not settled.

Status (16 Oct 2026). The physical kernel is implemented as wft.model.build_matrix_rc (opt-in through the rc_D_y hyper; production bundles are untouched and bit-identical). It is not frozen and the campaign re-pass is on hold until the X width question is answered or stated as a limitation. The detectors are no longer available: everything here, including what is open, works from data and simulation already in hand.

Generated by sps_beam_test_26/analysis/cloud_basics/make_model_deck.py.

The chamber: a drift gap, a 150 µm amplification gap, and a resistive layer cut into strips along y

MX17 readout board (from the gerbers). Hover the layers. Dotted terms and chart points have tooltips.

2

Details

The MX17 chambers are bulk micromegas with a 30 mm drift gap and two orthogonal readout views. A track ionises the gas; the electrons drift down to the mesh, multiply in the 150 µm amplification gap, and the avalanche charge lands on a resistive film. The film is not continuous: it is cut into strips 550 µm wide on a 0.80 mm pitch that run along y (mpgd26/scenes_chamber.py, from the board gerbers). Below it, through ~50 µm of insulator and the pads, are the Y readout strips (layer 5, they measure y) and the X readout strips (layer 6, one layer deeper, they measure x), both on a 0.78 mm pitch.

Two consequences drive the whole model. (1) The charge that lands on a resistive strip can flow along it, i.e. along y, as an RC line, but it cannot cross to the next resistive strip in x. So the Y view sees charge spread with time and the X view does not. (2) The footprint of one avalanche on the readout strips is set by the board (strip width, induction through the layers), not by the gas, and X, one layer deeper, sees it slightly wider than Y.

Each constant has its own measurement on head-on tracks: slides 4–10 take them one at a time.

3

Details

This is the whole model. Each 60 ns depth slice k of the track drifts for u_k and lands at p0 + w·u_k with a Gaussian width σ0² + 2·Dd·u_k. On Y, the landed charge then keeps spreading along the resistive strip with σ² growing by 2·D_rc per ns. The readout sees each increment of the charge above a strip through the electronics response; in the code (build_matrix_rc) the spread is evaluated at the time-since-landing edges RC_EDGES (0, 30, 60, …, 3000 ns), fine early, coarse late. The charge profile q_k is not modelled: NNLS solves it for every trial (p0, w, t0).

The hypers that switch it on are rc_D_y (presence enables the kernel), rc_D_x (default 0), sigma_p0_x/_y or sigma_p0, Dp = √(2·Dd), rc_tmpl (1 = X template for both views). Optional: lor_frac_<view>/lor_gamma_<view> (footprint tails, resolution-neutral, slide 17), rc_drain. None of c1, c2, kY, τ_s, σ_s is read.

What the model does not contain: attachment (needed on the beam only, slide 9), longitudinal diffusion, a field gradient, and anything that would explain the excess X width growth (slide 18).

Drift: electrons arrive in order of depth, and spread as √depth

Left: the mechanism. Right: det3 at 347 V/cm, Magboltz against what the chamber measures.

4

Details

Velocity. Each depth slice arrives after u = z / v, so arrival time is depth. v(E) comes from the calibration bundle of each chamber and run condition (bench 24.6–39.9 µm/ns; beam det4 14.3 / 8.2 / 4.9 µm/ns at 243 / 150 / 92 V/cm from the run_71 composition).

Diffusion. The transverse spread grows as σ² = D_T²·z = 2·Dd·u. Magboltz says water slows the drift and cools it: at 347 V/cm, the 1.0 % water that reproduces det3's measured v (34.9 µm/ns) would give D_T = 298 µm/√cm. The X head-on widths, where nothing else widens the cluster, say 438 ± 13, close to dry (483). The same holds on every bench chamber (slide 18).

The model's choice, for now: Dd is taken empirically from the X stack (≈ dry gas), per chamber, and a v-derived water fraction is never carried into D_T (FINDINGS §28–29). This is a decision forced by an open problem, not a resolution of it.

The water grid for Ar/iso 95/5 ends at 1 %, so det3's v-implied water sits on the grid edge (iso_fit.json row sat_det3: v 34.9, D_T 438 ± 13, Magboltz at that v 298). Gap 27.9 mm (dished cathode) is taken into account in v and D_T.

The avalanche spreads by 22–28 µm. The footprint the strips see is 14–22 times wider.

So σ0 is a readout constant: resistive-strip width, induction through the layers, inter-strip coupling. Water or dry, beam or bench, the gas cannot change it.

det4 reads the same on the bench and at the beam once the track inclination is cut out (0.36–0.40 mm). X is a little wider than Y, as the deeper X layer should be.

5

Details

The bench and beam calibrations used to disagree on the prompt width (σ_p0 0.39–0.43 mm on the bench, 0.15 mm on the beam with det4's beam kernel). That was bookkeeping: each fit put the same neighbour charge in a different parameter (FINDINGS §1). Measured model-free on head-on tracks, the leading-edge (first-charge) neighbour fraction is a detector property that does not move with the drift field.

The avalanche cannot make a 0.4 mm footprint: at 25–40 kV/cm Magboltz gives D_T 181–225 µm/√cm, so the 150 µm gap spreads it by 22–28 µm (magboltz_bench_dry_amp.json). The width comes from the board.

What the model takes: one σ0 per view per chamber. The joint fit at |tan| < 0.03 (the rcm arms) carries ~0.1 mm of track walk; tightening to 0.01 brings det4 to 0.365 and det3 to 0.372 mm, i.e. to det4's beam Y value (FINDINGS §28). X's footprint is wider than Y's by the board geometry (Y strips are layer 5, X strips layer 6), so the X/Y ratio should be a fixed geometric number rather than a free per-chamber knob. The X footprint also has tails beyond a Gaussian (pseudo-Voigt, FINDINGS §23); they are real but do not move the resolution.

Y: the landed charge keeps spreading along the resistive strip, as an RC line

Left: the mechanism. Right: what each Y strip holds as time passes, at det4's beam values.

6

Details

The avalanche charge lands on a resistive strip and drains through it. Along the strip the film is a distributed RC line: the charge density obeys a diffusion equation with D_rc = 1/(R_s·c), so a landed Gaussian keeps its shape and widens as σ² = σ0² + 2·D_rc·s, s the time since landing (Dixit et al., NIM A 518 (2004) 721; for strips, Galan et al., JINST 7 (2012) C04009; references in wft/REFERENCES.md). Each readout strip sees its fraction of that charge change with time, and the electronics see every increment.

The resistive strips run along y. The Y readout strips cross them, so they see the spread. The X readout strips run along the resistive strips, so moving charge along y keeps it over the same X strip, and charge cannot jump to the next resistive strip in x. X therefore has no RC term, which is what the data say (next slide).

Under this mechanism there are no discrete copies. Charge reaches ±2 only by passing ±1, so ±2 always holds less than ±1 and starts later, while late in the pulse it comes close (curves). That is the ordering the old c2 < c1 rule tried to impose by hand (slide 13).

Constants drawn: det4 at the beam, σ0,y = 0.41 mm (mean of three fields) and D_rc = 2.16×10⁻⁴ mm²/ns (run_71 RC fit with Magboltz drift diffusion, 2.08 / 2.08 / 1.94×10⁻⁴ at 243/150/92 V/cm, ÷ 0.94 for the attachment loss, FINDINGS §27).

One constant per chamber fits Y 1.7–3.3× better. On X the RC term buys almost nothing and fits 7–26× smaller than on Y: there is no resistive spread across the strips.

7

Details

rc_diffusion.py fits each view of each dataset with W_o(t) = S(t) ⊗ dF_o/ds, where S is the all-strip sum (it carries the electronics and the arrival current, taken from the data, no template), and F_o the fraction over strip offset o of a Gaussian with σ² = σ0² + 2·D_rc·s. One free D_rc per view. Unbiased stacks (fixed threshold, no per-event normalisation, FINDINGS §10).

This fit has no drift-diffusion term. On the bench, where the drift spreads the charge too, it absorbs part of the drift growth into D_rc, so its bench Y numbers (5–9×10⁻⁴) are higher than the joint X+Y fit the model actually uses (2.8–7.9×10⁻⁴, slide 10), where X pins the drift diffusion. On the beam the drift spread is 2–3× smaller and the two agree (2.0–2.3 vs 1.9–2.1×10⁻⁴). The point of this slide is the contrast between views, which survives either way.

D_rc differs from chamber to chamber (det4 lowest, det7 highest): a construction constant of each board's resistive film. det4 bench and beam agree within 1.2–1.4× once the bench drift diffusion is fitted jointly (FINDINGS §28).

Electronics: the clean X template drives both views

The measured single-strip impulse responses of det3 (production bundle), normalised to their peak.

X template

Y template

Both views are read by the same DREAM chips with the same settings: their electronics are identical.

Yet Y dips to -8 % and X only to -2 %: the extra dip is charge leaving the strip along the resistive layer, already inside Y's "impulse response".

So the model uses the X template for both views (rc_tmpl = 1) and adds the RC spread explicitly, instead of counting it twice.

8

Details

The template is the response of one strip to charge arriving on it at t = 0: DREAM preamplifier and shaper (peaking ~180 ns, the same on bench and beam) plus the ion tail. It is measured, not modelled (wft.calibrate.measure_templates): the brightest strip of inclined bench tracks, which also contains the strip's own short depth segment. Beam bundles reused the bench template.

A clean electronics response for a 60 ns sampled DREAM channel has a small undershoot; X shows -2.3 %. Y shows -8.4 %, and the difference has the sign and size of charge spreading away from the strip after it lands. Since the electronics are the same, that part belongs to the RC term, and the physical kernel uses the X template for both views (rc_tmpl = 1 or 'x'). Templates are per chamber (each bundle has its own); det3 is drawn.

Source: calib_bundle_r06/arrays.npz of sat_det3 (tmpl_x, tmpl_y, 10 ns grid).

Per run: the beam O₂ moved over hours. Water does not attach.

9

Details

Beam. The late charge in det4's run_71 falls at the same rate per unit time at all three drift fields, in both views, with no electronics undershoot after the drift ends (FINDINGS §16). Only loss of drifting electrons does that, and Magboltz puts it on O₂: one composition, 1.51 % water and 0.078 % air (163 ppm O₂), fits all three fields and both views with no free loss rate. At 243 V/cm that is η·v = 2.20×10⁻⁴/ns, and 63% of the electrons from the cathode arrive (33% at 92 V/cm). The O₂ was not constant: run_63 the night before went from 230 to 147 ppm over hours, and the CO₂ period on 1 Aug was ~290 ppm. The absolute ppm scale depends on Magboltz's three-body O₂ attachment and is uncertain by a factor of a few; the beam/bench contrast is not.

Bench. The det3 drift scan (35–382 V/cm) stays flat to ±2 % for 1.2 µs of drift at the two lowest fields, where a beam-like loss would remove ~14 %. The same physics model gives 0.95 % water and no air (≲ 10 ppm O₂).

In the model. The forward model has no attachment term today. The bench needs none. A beam reconstruction would need one per run (η·v from the composition, or the measured rate). The SPS constants the bench model takes (σ0, D_rc) are shifted by the beam loss by ≤ 7 % (injection test, FINDINGS §27).

Full study: notes/mx17-attachment-slides and notes/mx17-beam-attachment; FINDINGS §16–27.

10

Details

The bench constants are those of the rcm arms (make_rc_arms.py from results/bench_uniform.json, Dd free), which is what the held-out comparison in slide 16 ran. Converted: σ_p0 = σ0, Dp = √(2·Dd), rc_D_y = D_rc. The latest joint fits (FINDINGS §28, bench_pinrc.py) agree: D_rc det2 4.2, det3 2.8, det6 7.9, det7 5.7×10⁻⁴; det4 2.57×10⁻⁴ free or 2.2 pinned to the beam at no cost in the stack (+0.3 % rms) or the held-out angles (±0.03°).

Decided, not frozen: det4 takes D_rc from the beam, the other chambers keep their bench value; Dd per chamber from the joint fit (≈ dry); σ0 should come from the tight-|tan| stack (it carries ~0.1 mm of track walk at 0.03). None of these choices moves det4's held-out resolution by more than ±0.04°. Freezing waits on the X width question (slide 18).

The beam column is for completeness. No beam bundle has been rebuilt with this kernel; the beam bundles still carry the old copy kernel and the H4 v/Dp.

Old vs new: delayed copies, or one cloud that keeps spreading

det3, Y view, one unit charge landing on the centre strip: the mechanism and the strip waveforms it predicts.

11

Details

Old (production r06, delay form; wft.model.build_matrix). Each strip receives its own prompt fraction of a Gaussian (σ_p0 = 0.425 mm, plus Dp²·u with drift time) through its own view's template, plus a copy of each ±1 neighbour's fraction scaled by c1·kY (0.050 × 2.88 on Y) and delayed by τ_s = 166 ns, and of each ±2 neighbour's by c2·kY (c2/c1 = 0.60) at 2·τ_s, both smeared by σ_s = 9 ns. On X the copies are the same with kY → 1. The lp share mode (an RC-dispersed copy instead of a delayed one) was used for the beam studies.

New (build_matrix_rc). One Gaussian of σ0 = 0.410 mm (+ 2·Dd·u) lands; on Y it widens as 2·D_rc·s with D_rc = 2.78×10⁻⁴ mm²/ns, and every strip sees its share change through the X template. ±1 and ±2 start at once (their prompt share) and keep rising for microseconds; ±2 always stays below ±1. In the old kernel the neighbours' extra charge arrives as a short pulse at a fixed delay.

The centre strip is drawn at a third of its height. Both columns use det3's production and rcm constants. The waveforms are a single landing; a real track adds up 18 such landings along its depth.

The old constants were fitted on bench cosmics by the angle χ² (wft.calibrate.fit_hypers), not taken from the detector physics. Several directions in that χ² are flat, so the fit could wander (c2 > c1 on every bundle shipped before 21 Aug).

The new constants come from head-on stacks, where every depth lands on the same strips and the neighbour signal is pure lateral spread. None is tuned against the reference angle.

12

Details

Production bundles and share modes: det2 delay (calib_bundle_r06), det3 delay (calib_bundle_r06), det4 delay (loader default) (calib_bundle_lp_t0p), det6 delay (loader default) (calib_bundle_lp), det7 delay (calib_bundle_r06). The det4/det6 bundles are named "_lp" but carry no share_mode field, so the loader's default ('delay') applies; their share_lp hyper is not read by the model.

The old σ_p0 and Dp are not one-to-one with σ0 and Dd: the copy kernel also put neighbour charge in c1·kY, so the three pieces were traded against each other by the fit (det6's production bundle has σ_p0 = 0.039 mm and Dp = 0.0016, i.e. almost all its spread in the copies). The new kernel has one place for each piece of physics.

Code: wft/model.py (build_matrix old, build_matrix_rc new, selected by the presence of rc_D_y), wft/calib.py (HYPER_NAMES, effective_c2, check_kernel_ordering).

The c2 < c1 problem disappears: there is no ratio left to fit

Left: the ±2/±1 copy ratio the bundles carried. Right: under RC spreading, ±2 always holds less than ±1.

13

Details

Physically, charge reaches the ±2 strip only through the ±1, so a copy kernel needs c2 < c1. The cosmic χ² is flat in that direction, and every bundle shipped before 21 Aug 2026 had walked to c2 > c1 (det3 1.14, det2 1.53, det7 1.75, det4 2.12); all of them and every product built on them were retired (mx_june_wft/RETIRE_C2GTC1_2026-08-21.md). Since then wft.calib.check_kernel_ordering refuses an inverted bundle at load, save and install, and r06 pins c2 = 0.6·c1.

That gate is a rule imposed on a parameterisation that cannot express the physics. The data themselves are not a fixed ratio: on the beam, Y's delayed component reaches ±2 about as strongly as ±1 (decomposition b1 = 0.22, b2 = 0.22 at 243 V/cm, FINDINGS §2), which a copy kernel with c2 < c1 cannot draw and RC spreading draws naturally: late in the pulse ±2 approaches ±1 (right), while the total on ±2 is always below ±1 because a widening Gaussian centred on strip 0 always puts less charge further out.

In the physical kernel there is no c2: the gate has nothing to check. (The per-view ratio study of 9 Oct, which pinned c2/c1_y = 0.95, is superseded by this.)

The old Dp was about half the measured diffusion; the fit made up the width elsewhere

Left: det3, lateral width against depth under each description. Right: D_T implied by each, all chambers.

old Dp

new Dd

Magboltz dry

14

Details

The production Dp (0.014–0.016 mm/√ns on det2/3/4/7) converts to D_T = Dp/√v ≈ 237–280 µm/√cm, 0.48–0.55× of what the X head-on widths measure and about half of dry Magboltz (FINDINGS §6). det6's production bundle has almost no drift term at all (Dp = 0.0016).

The bench calibration put c1 near its floor (0.05) and loaded the neighbour charge into a constant σ_p0 (0.39–0.43 mm) and the copies. On head-on bench data alone, the prompt width, the drift diffusion and the drift length are degenerate (det3 σ0 moves 0.36 ↔ 0.48 while Dd moves ×5, FINDINGS §6), so the angle χ² could settle anywhere along that valley. The new model breaks the degeneracy with a joint X+Y fit: X has no RC term, so X's width growth with depth is drift diffusion alone.

Left panel: the old model is too narrow for deep charge and similar for shallow charge; the new one follows the dry curve. The orange curve is what the gas model would predict from v: that is the open X width excess (slide 18).

τ_s was a fitted compromise, 2.5–7× faster than the spreading it stood for

Time scales of the neighbour signal: the old kernel's delay against direct measurements and the RC constants.

The fitted copy delay τ_s sits at 105–166 ns on every chamber.

Measured directly, the Y neighbour signal builds up over 410–710 ns, and the RC constants put one pitch of spreading at hundreds of ns to over a microsecond.

A single delayed copy cannot follow a √t spread. The χ² picked the compromise that fits the early part of the pulse; the late part was misfit, seen as "Y copies too early on the beam".

15

Details

tau_s and sigma_s (and c1, c2, kY) were fitted on bench cosmics by wft.calibrate.fit_hypers; they do not come from simulation. One value serves both views. Direct waveform measurements give much slower spreading: 410 ns on the det3 bench for Y (230 ns for X, HANDOFF_2026-07-30), and 530–710 ns on the beam (decomposition into a prompt part plus a low-passed copy of the centre strip, decompose.py; X has no delayed part at all on the beam).

The two closure failures logged earlier, "Y copies 13–15σ too early on the beam" and "Y ±2 delay too short on the bench", are the same defect seen twice: the copy form has one delay, the physics has a continuum (FINDINGS §4).

The "pitch² / 2·D_rc" rows are not a fitted time constant: they are the time it takes the RC spread alone to widen the cloud by one readout pitch in quadrature, a natural scale of the mechanism. The bench decomposition is not shown: there the drift diffusion makes the neighbour/centre ratio grow through the pulse and the decomposition is unphysical for X (FINDINGS §2).

Held out, no refit: Y better on all five chambers, X mixed

Paired change in the scale-corrected s68 angle resolution, physical kernel (rcm) − production, 2000 events per chamber.

filled: all tracks · open: head-on

better by > 2σ

worse by > 2σ

within 2σ

16

Details

Test. make_rc_arms.py → plane_bench.py (2000 held-out events per golden run, the same events for both kernels) → compare_bench.py --start blind (results/compare_bench_rc.json). The physical kernel takes every constant from the head-on measurement and is not refitted against the reference. The comparison is scale-corrected: each arm's tan is divided by its own slope against M3 before s68 is taken, because the rc arms read angles 3–8 % flat (the bundle v and the per-chamber angle scale kw were calibrated under the old kernel).

Y improves everywhere: det2 -0.15 / -0.36°; det3 -0.09 / -0.14°; det4 -0.15 / -0.20°; det6 -0.55 / -0.90°; det7 -0.12 / -0.28° (all / head-on). The head-on gain is the largest, where the old kernel's copy timing mattered most.

X: neutral on det2/det3, better on det6/det7, worse on det4 over all tracks (+0.16 ± 0.05°). The X χ²/dof is worse than production on every chamber (det3 61 → 84, det2 110 → 189): the model's X is missing something that production's small X copies were absorbing. The ref start agrees (det2 Y −0.10/−0.30, det6 Y −0.27/−0.70, det4 X +0.09).

X is not closed: refits, an X RC term and footprint tails barely move it

Paired X change against production on the held-out bench, for every X variant tried (condor 4410535, 4410788).

rcm: measured, no refit

rcf3: σ0,x, σ0,y, D_rc,y refitted

rcf4x: + D_rc,x free

rcfD: + Dp free

rcmlor: + footprint tails

rcmlor2: tails, variant

Refitting the physical constants, freeing an X RC term, freeing the drift diffusion, or adding footprint tails: none moves X by more than its error, except rcfD on det4.

det4 X stays +0.16° worse. det4's amplification stripes run across X, a gain pattern a uniform-gain model cannot represent: an untested hypothesis.

Freeing Dp brings back the degeneracy: Dp drops to 0.013–0.022 and σ0 inflates to 0.45–0.75 mm for a 1–2 % χ² gain. The fit uses the footprint to absorb a deficiency.

17

Details

Arms (all from recal.py seeded from rcm, benched paired against production; results/compare_bench_rc.json, compare_bench_lor.json): rcf3 refits σ0,x, σ0,y and D_rc,y; rcf4x adds D_rc,x (it fits to 0–1.2×10⁻⁵, against 3.6–5.9×10⁻⁴ for Y, so rcf4x ≡ rcf3); rcfD frees Dp too; rcmlor/rcmlor2 replace part of the prompt Gaussian by a Lorentzian (pseudo-Voigt tails, η 0.10–0.36, γ 0.53–0.91 mm), which improves the head-on profile χ² by 17–37 % but not the angle.

Also rejected for X: charge snapping to the 550 µm resistive-strip centres (no 0.80 mm periodicity in X centroids, Rayleigh power 0.2–1.7 where ~1 is noise, FINDINGS §23).

What remains open on X: (1) the excess width growth (next slide), which the model takes empirically but does not explain; (2) det4's X deficit. Both can be pursued on data in hand: det4's gain map against its stripes exists from the bench, and a position-dependent gain can be written into the model and benched on the same held-out events.

Open: X widens like dry gas, though v says the gas is wet

X diffusion from head-on stacks against Magboltz, every dataset. No Ar/iso/water mix fits det3's field scan (χ² 80/36).

measured, X head-on

Magboltz at the gas v implies

Magboltz dry

18

Details

The observation (FINDINGS §29, report ~/x17/cosmic_bench/cloud_basics/xwidth/report.html). On every bench dataset X widens with depth at D_T 400–520 µm/√cm. Ar/iso 95/5 with the water each run's v needs gives 270–325. The excess, in quadrature, is ~300–430 µm/√cm on every chamber. It does not depend on gain (det3, mesh 425–505 V), covers the whole active area with no hot spot, lands at the anode (no X undershoot, D_rc,x → 0) and is not track inclination. It is closer to per-depth than per-time (det6/det7 0.86 ± 0.11 against 1.16 for per-time). The beam has it too (+118, +143, +286 in quadrature at 243 / 150 / 92 V/cm; indicative only, at 92 V/cm the drift is 3× the window and no beam template exists, so the fit is template-free).

Not the gas at any composition tried: Ar/iso 0.5–8 % × water 0–1.5 %, seven fields (condor 4440949/4440956). An iso-poor gas can match one single-field chamber, but not det6 and not det3's five fields together (best χ² 80/36 at iso 1.5 %, water 0.9375 %).

Two readings remain: (1) Magboltz's water model: water slows the drift as predicted but cools the transverse energy less; both setups are wet. (2) A non-gas lateral term linear in depth, which no current model has.

For the model, meanwhile: Dd from the X stack (≈ dry), never from v.

What is open, and what this does not rule out

  • The X width excess. Unexplained. Checks left, all on data or simulation in hand: a joint X+Y fit on the det3 drift-scan Y view (the caches hold it), where Dd is shared with the RC term; the same mixtures with another cross-section set or published Ar/iso/H₂O D_T data; other contaminants (N₂, CO₂) in the Magboltz grid; the beam X with a proper template re-extracted from run_71, and the 25.6° runs as a known-angle cross-check. If they cannot separate the two readings, it is stated as a limitation and Dd stays empirical.
  • det4's X deficit. +0.16 ± 0.05° against production. Hypothesis: its amplification stripes across X. Testable with the bench gain map and a position-dependent gain in the model, benched on the same held-out events.
  • X χ² worse everywhere. Even where the X angle is unchanged or better: something production's small X copies absorbed is missing (likely the same physics as the width excess).
  • Angle scale. The rc arms read angles 3–8 % flat; the bundle v and kw were calibrated under the old kernel and must be re-derived with the new one before any absolute angle is quoted.
  • Edge widths. The early (prompt) X width doubles in ⟨x²⟩ at the chamber edges: a separate footprint / field effect, visible in the existing position maps.

Not yet settled

  • The kernel is not frozen: det4 D_rc from the beam, others from the bench; Dd from the joint fit; σ0 from the tight-|tan| stack. Then the full gate.
  • The re-pass is on hold: until the X width question is answered or written down as a limitation.
  • Beam bundles: still carry the old copy kernel and H4 v/Dp; a beam model would also need attachment per run.

The detectors are no longer available: every item above is answered from existing data and simulation, or stated as a limitation.

19

Details

What the held-out result does not show: that the physical kernel is better in absolute angle (it is compared after scale correction), that it transfers to the n_TOF campaign (different chambers' conditions, gas line and trigger; it has not been run there), or that the X description is right (it is not yet).

Retracted along the way and not to be revived: bench attachment (a max-normalised stacking artefact, FINDINGS §10), the field-ordered "leading spike" (threshold alignment, §14), the per-view c2/c1_y = 0.95 re-pass (superseded).

All numbers: sps_beam_test_26/analysis/cloud_basics/FINDINGS.md §1–29; HANDOFF.md, "Detector model basics" and "X width excess".
